Founded in 1881 by [[Kintarō Hattori]] in [[Tokyo]], Seiko introduced the world's first commercial [[Quartz clock|quartz wristwatch]] in 1969.{{cite web|url=https://www.watchtime.com/featured/timepiece-timeline-milestone-seiko-watches/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211125080218/https://www.watchtime.com/featured/timepiece-timeline-milestone-seiko-watches/|title=The History of Seiko Through 12 Milestone Seiko Watches|publisher=EBNER PUBLISHING INTERNATIONAL, INC.|date=20 January 2021|archive-date=25 November 2021}}{{cite web|url=https://www.seikowatches.com/global-en/special/heritage/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220403072946/https://www.seikowatches.com/global-en/special/heritage/|title=Our Heritage|publisher=Seiko Watch Corporation|archive-date=3 April 2022}} Seiko is widely known for its wristwatches.{{cite news|url=https://www.ft.com/content/9f95d770-31f1-11e5-91ac-a5e17d9b4cff|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191001141252/https://www.ft.com/content/9f95d770-31f1-11e5-91ac-a5e17d9b4cff|title=Seiko sets its sights on high-quality mechanical market|newspaper=Financial Times|date=September 28, 2015 |archive-date=1 October 2019|access-date=18 January 2022}} Seiko and [[Rolex]] are the only two [[watch]] companies considered to be [[Vertical integration|vertically integrated]].{{cite web|url=https://www.gearpatrol.com/watches/a419348/seiko-watch-factory-photo-tour/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221203101111/https://www.gearpatrol.com/watches/a419348/seiko-watch-factory-photo-tour/|title=Go Behind the Scenes of One of the Most Impressive Watchmaking Operations in the World|publisher=Gear Patrol, LLC.|date=8 February 2018|archive-date=3 December 2022|access-date=3 February 2023}} Seiko is able to design and develop all the components of a watch, as well as assemble, adjust, inspect and ship them in-house. Seiko's [[mechanical watch]]es consist of approximately 200 parts, and the company has the technology and production facilities to design and manufacture all of these parts internally.{{cite web|url=https://www.seiko.co.jp/recruit/graduate/quality/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230203074216/https://www.seiko.co.jp/recruit/graduate/quality/|title=Seiko Quality|language=ja|publisher=Seiko Group Corporation|archive-date=3 February 2023|access-date=3 February 2023}} The company was incorporated (K. Hattori & Co., Ltd.) in 1917 and renamed Hattori Seiko Co., Ltd. in 1983 and Seiko Corporation in 1997. After reconstructing and creating its operating subsidiaries (such as Seiko Watch Corporation and Seiko Clock Inc.), it became a [[holding company]] in 2001 and was renamed Seiko Holdings Corporation on July 1, 2007. Seiko Holdings Corporation was renamed Seiko Group Corporation as of October 1, 2022.{{cite press release | date = 2022-05-10 | title = 商号の変更および定款の一部変更に関するお知らせ | trans-title = Announcement of Change in Trade Name and Partial Amendment to Articles of Incorporation | url = https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/8050/ir_material3/182770/00.pdf | language = ja | location = | agency = Grand 2010–2022 andy low | publisher = Seiko Holdings Corporation | access-date = 2022-05-11 }} Seiko watches were originally produced by two Hattori family companies (not subsidiaries of K. Hattori & Co); one was [[Seikosha|Daini Seikosha Co.]] (now known as Seiko Instruments Inc., a subsidiary of Seiko Holdings since 2009) and the other was [[Seikosha|Suwa Seikosha Co.]] (now known as [[Epson|Seiko Epson Corporation]], an independent publicly traded company). Having two companies both producing the same brand of watch enabled Seiko to improve technology through [[Competition (companies)|competition]] and hedge [[Risk management|risk]]. It also reduced risk of production problems, since one company can increase production in the case of decreased production in the other parties. Seiko remains as one of the world's most recognised watchmaking brands.{{cite web|url=https://www.j-paris.co.jp/content/column/6558|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210224211935/https://www.j-paris.co.jp/content/column/6558|script-title=ja:文字板に込めた、それぞれの製造地への想い|language=ja|publisher=Jewelry Paris Inc.|date=12 February 2021|archive-date=24 February 2021|access-date=3 February 2023}} In Ginza, where the company was founded, there are several Seiko-related facilities in addition to Seiko House Ginza, including the Seiko Museum and Seiko Dream Square.{{cite web|url=https://timeandtidewatches.com/grand-seiko-manufacture-series-part-2-the-seiko-museum-in-ginza/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230813020348/https://timeandtidewatches.com/grand-seiko-manufacture-series-part-2-the-seiko-museum-in-ginza/|title=Grand Seiko Manufacture Tour Part 2: The Seiko Museum in Ginza|publisher=Time and Tide Watches|date=July 23, 2023|archive-date=13 August 2023}} Several Seiko boutiques and department stores in the area frequently offer Ginza-exclusive models.{{cite web|url=https://www.seikowatches.com/jp-ja/special/ginza_limited/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250214191108/https://www.seikowatches.com/jp-ja/special/ginza_limited/|title=Ginza Limited Edition|publisher=Seiko|date=|archive-date=14 February 2025}} ==History== === 1881 founding to 1929 === [[File:K. Hattori.jpg|thumb|Portrait of [[Kintarō Hattori]], 1916]] In 1881, Seiko founder Kintarō Hattori opened a watch and jewelry shop called "K. Hattori" ({{lang|ja|服部時計店}}) in Tokyo.{{Cite news |title=History of Seiko and Its Products |language=en |work=The Seiko Museum |url=http://museum.seiko.co.jp/en/history/company/index.html |access-date=2017-10-14}} Kintarō Hattori had been working as clockmaker apprentice since the age of 13, with multiple stints in different watch shops, such as “Kobayashi Clock Shop”, run by an expert technician named Seijiro Sakurai; “Kameda Clock Shop” in Nihonbashi; and “Sakata Clock Shop” in Ueno, where he learned how to both sell and repair timepieces. Around the time of Seiko's founding, watchmakers in Tokyo, [[Osaka]], and [[Nagoya]] were studying and producing [[pocket watch]]es based on Western products. Japanese wholesalers needed to purchase all the imported timepieces from foreign trading companies established in [[Yokohama]], [[Kobe]], and other open port areas.[https://museum.seiko.co.jp/en/seiko_history/founder/founder/001// Historical references, Ginza Museum][https://museum.seiko.co.jp/en/seiko_history/founder/founder/002// Spirit of Kintaro Hattori, the Founder (SEIKO)] In 1885, Hattori began dealing directly with these foreign trading firms in the Yokohama settlement focused on the wholesaling and retailing of western (imported) timepieces and machinery.[https://museum.seiko.co.jp/en/seiko_history/founder/founder/004// Impact of the western companies of Yokohama] Over the years, Hattori developed a close partnership with multiple foreign trading firms, including C&J Favre-Brandt, [[François Perregaux|F. Perregaux & Co.]], [[Zanuti|Zanuti & Cie.]] and Siber & Brennwald, allowing him to obtain exclusive imported timepieces and machinery, which was not available elsewhere at that time.[https://museum.seiko.co.jp/en/knowledge/relation_08// Foreign trading firms in Yokohama][https://museum.seiko.co.jp/en/seiko_history/founder/founder/003// Historical references from 1860 to 1880][https://museum.seiko.co.jp/en/seiko_history/founder/founder/004// K. Hattori & Co. (1881–1891)][https://museum.seiko.co.jp/en/seiko_history/founder/founder/005// Episode 3 (1892) Seikosha Factory] Hattori's shop became increasingly popular due to the rarity of the imported watches the shop was selling, which were not found anywhere else in Japan. The growing success allowed him to relocate the company to the main street of [[Ginza]] (Tokyo), still the epicenter of commerce in Japan to this day. In 1891, 10 years after the establishment of K. Hattori & Co., the 31-year-old Kintaro was appointed director of the Tokyo Clockmaker and Watchmaker Association and member of Tokyo Chamber of Commerce. In 1892, Hattori began to produce clocks under the name {{Nihongo|[[Seikosha]]|{{linktext|精工|舎}}|Seikōsha}}, meaning, roughly, "House of Exquisite Workmanship." According to Seiko's official company history, titled ''A Journey In Time: The Remarkable Story of Seiko'' (2003), Seiko is a Japanese word meaning {{nihongo|"exquisite"|{{linktext|精巧}}|Seikō}}; it is homophonous with the word for {{nihongo|"success"|{{linktext|成功}}|Seikō}}.{{cite book|title=A Journey In Time: The Remarkable Story of Seiko|page=9|author=John Goodall|publisher=Seiko Watch Corporation|date=2003}} In 1895, the watch dealer purchased the corner of Ginza 4-chome (the present-day location of [[Wako (retailer)|WAKO]]), and constructed a building with a clock tower (16 meters from top to bottom), setting up shop at the new address. Seiko launched its first in-house pocket watch, the Timekeeper, in 1895; the first Japanese-made wristwatch, the Laurel, in 1913; and the first Seiko-branded wristwatch in 1924. Wristwatches and pocket watches completed in 1923 were provisionally given the name "Glory." However, since its pronunciation was similar to "gorori" (ゴロリ), a Japanese onomatopoeia for tumbling, which was considered unlucky, it was decided that the brand name for watches to be mass-produced from 1924 would be "Seiko."{{cite web|url=https://mainichi.jp/articles/20240130/oog/00m/020/003000c|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240621024106/https://mainichi.jp/articles/20240130/oog/00m/020/003000c|script-title=ja:セイコー/19　自社製時計の名称をセイコーに統一＝広岩近広|language=ja|publisher= [[Mainichi Shimbun]]|date=|archive-date=21 June 2024|access-date=}} In 1929, the Seiko pocket watch was adopted as the official watch for the drivers of [[Ministry of Railways (Japan)|Japanese Government Railway]]s. === 1930 to 1990 === Military watches, notably the "Seikosha Type 93 Tensoku-Dokei" produced for Japanese troops during [[World War II]] were manufactured by Seiko, which by 1938, produced 1.2 million timepieces a year.{{cite web | title=Flieger Friday: Seikosha Kamikaze – Flieger Friday | url=https://fliegerfriday.com/flieger-friday-seikosha-kamikaze/ }}{{Cite web |date=2022-04-19 |title=The Imperial Japanese Navy ‘Air Soldier’ Weems |url=https://flightbirds.net/the-imperial-japanese-navy-air-soldier-weems/ |access-date=2026-06-08 |website=Flight Birds |language=en-US}} The scarcity of raw materials during the war diverted much of Seiko's production to on-board instruments for military aircraft and ships. In contrast to Japan, Germany utilized both domestically produced and Swiss-produced watches.{{cite web | title=This is the Seiko Watch Made for Japanese Pilots During WWII | date=September 12, 2019 | url=https://www.gearpatrol.com/watches/a613700/watches-you-should-know-seikosha-tensoku-kamikaze/ }} Japan's isolation in the Pacific meant the country could not rely on importing foreign timepieces.{{Cite web |last=Love |first=Zen |date=2019-09-12 |title=This Is the Seiko Watch Made for Japanese Pilots During WWII |url=http://gearpatrol.com/watches/a613700/watches-you-should-know-seikosha-tensoku-kamikaze/ |access-date=2022-10-02 |website=Gear Patrol |language=en-US}} [[File:Ginza_in_1933.JPG|thumb|Seiko Group in 1933]] In 1951, Seiko broadcast its first radio commercial in Japan, and when Japan's first commercial television station opened in 1953, it broadcast Japan's first television commercial. The first Japanese commercial was supposed to be broadcast as a time signal at noon, but the video technician mishandled the equipment and the commercial lasted only three seconds, and it was rebroadcast at 7:00 p.m. the same day.{{cite web|url=https://www.seikowatches.com/jp-ja/special/heritage|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221204180104/https://www.seikowatches.com/jp-ja/special/heritage|script-title=ja:セイコー腕時計の歴史|language=ja|publisher=Seiko Watch Corporation|archive-date=4 December 2022|access-date=3 February 2023}} In 1956, Seiko launched Japan's first [[Automatic watch|automatic wristwatch]], the Automatic. The retail price at the time was 13,500 yen, more than three times the price of men's wristwatches, which were generally in the 4,000 yen range. In the same year, the company released the Marvel, which represented a significant improvement in accuracy, quality, and productivity over the previous model. This was achieved by increasing the outer diameter of the movement compared to the previous model. In 1958, Seiko developed the 'Dia-Shock' anti-shock device. In 1959, Seiko launched the Gyro Marvel, which featured a revolutionary self-winding mechanism, the Magic Lever, developed by Seiko. The Magic Lever was simple in structure and had high winding performance, and popularized automatic watches among the general public. In 1960, Seiko released the [[Grand Seiko]], aimed to be the most accurate wristwatch in the world. Seiko quickly developed quartz technology in preparation for the [[1964 Summer Olympics|1964 Tokyo Olympics]], and in 1963 launched the Seiko Crystal Chronometer, a dramatically smaller version of its previous quartz clock. The quartz clock Seiko had supplied to a broadcasting station in 1959 was about the size of a wardrobe, but this new product ran on two batteries and was portable. At the Tokyo Olympics, Seiko's mechanical stopwatches were selected as the official Olympic watches due to their high accuracy. Seiko launched Japan's first [[chronograph]] wristwatch, the Crown Chronograph, in 1964, Japan's first world time wristwatch in the same year, and Japan's first diver's wristwatch in 1965. In 1967, Japan's first diver's watch with 300m water resistance was launched. In 1967, Seiko won second and third place in a watch accuracy competition at a [[Neuchâtel Observatory]] competition; the competition was canceled after that year.{{cite web|url=https://museum.seiko.co.jp/en/seiko_history/milestone/milestone_04/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220403084500/https://museum.seiko.co.jp/en/seiko_history/milestone/milestone_04/|title=Technical Challenges at the Observatory Chronometer Competition in Switzerland|publisher=Seiko Holdings Corporation.|archive-date=3 April 2022}} In 1968, Seiko took first place in a [[Geneva Observatory]] competition with a score of 58.19, surpassing all previous records. Swiss companies ranked first to third for their quartz movements and Seiko ranked fourth to tenth for its mechanical movements. In the competition, there were special movements for the competition. {{multiple image | align = right | total_width = 230 | image1 = Seiko Astron.jpg | alt1 = Seiko Astron | caption1 = | image2 = Seiko 35A.jpg | alt2 = Caliber 35A, Nr. 00234 | caption2 = | footer = Quartz wristwatch movement Caliber 35A (right) developed by [[Seiko Epson|Suwa Seikosha]] in 1969, used in the [[Astron (wristwatch)|Seiko Astron]] (left) }} In 1969, Seiko released several wristwatches that the company now regards as historically significant models. The [[Astron (wristwatch)|Astron]] became the world’s first commercially available [[Quartz clock|quartz wristwatch]], with a price tag comparable to that of a mid-sized car at the time. The release of the Astron triggered what became known as the "Quartz Revolution" or "[[Quartz crisis|Quartz Crisis]]," during which the Swiss watch industry suffered a major decline from the 1970s through the early 1980s.{{Cite web|url=https://www.hodinkee.com/articles/four-revolutions-quartz-revolution|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190530193005/https://www.hodinkee.com/articles/four-revolutions-quartz-revolution|title=Four Revolutions: Part 1: A Concise History Of The Quartz Revolution|first=Joe|last=Thompson|website=Hodinkee|date=10 October 2017|archive-date=30 May 2019}}{{Cite web|url=https://museum.seiko.co.jp/en/knowledge/relation/relation_11/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306043210/https://museum.seiko.co.jp/en/knowledge/relation/relation_11/index.html|title=The Quartz Crisis and Recovery of Swiss Watches|website=The Seiko Museum|archive-date=6 March 2019}} The 5 Sports Speed Timer was the world’s first commercially available automatic chronograph, achieving great success due to its compact design and practical functionality. Although [[Zenith (watchmaker)|Zenith]] had previously unveiled a prototype automatic chronograph, Seiko was the first to bring one to market. Seiko also introduced the Grand Seiko V.F.A. (Very Fine Adjusted),{{Cite web |title=A new era in the history of Grand Seiko begins with Spring Drive U.F.A. |url=https://www.grand-seiko.com/us-en/news/2025/pr/20250401_SpringDrive |access-date=2026-06-08 |website=Grand Seiko |language=en-us}} a mechanical watch with ultra-high accuracy rated at ±2 seconds per day, and the U.T.D. (Ultra Thin Dress), a mechanical watch with an exceptionally thin movement measuring just 1.98 mm.{{cite web|url=https://www.watchtime.com/featured/seiko-a-chronograph-chronology/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250425220530/https://www.watchtime.com/featured/seiko-a-chronograph-chronology/|title=Seiko: A Chronograph Chronology|publisher=Watch Time|date=10 May 2024|archive-date=25 April 2025|access-date=25 April 2025}} Since the 1970s, Seiko has introduced a variety of wristwatches with various world firsts: in 1973, Seiko introduced the world's first wristwatch with a LCD display capable of displaying six digits for hours, minutes and seconds; in 1975, Seiko introduced the world's first digital watch with a stopwatch function and a diver's watch with a titanium case. In 1978, Seiko introduced the world's first quartz diver's watch with a water resistance of 600 meters; in 1982, the world's first wristwatch with a television; in 1983, the world's first wristwatch with a record-and-play function and an analog quartz chronograph; in 1984, the world's first wristwatch computer; and in 1986, the world's first diver's watch with a ceramic case water-resistant to 1000 meters. In 1974, Seiko launched Credor, a luxury brand using precious metals and jewelry, and in 1979, Alba, a low-priced brand for young people. In 1985, [[Orient Watch|Orient]] and Seiko established a joint factory. In 1986, [[Baselworld]] allowed non-European manufacturers to participate, and Seiko began exhibiting that year. [[File:Seiko Kinetic SMY151P1 watch.jpg|thumb|Kinetic SMY151P1]] In 1988, Seiko invented the world's first wristwatch with an innovative mechanism called "Auto Quartz", in which a rotating oscillating weight rotates in response to the wearer's arm movements, generating electricity to power the quartz. This mechanism was developed with the aim of creating a quartz watch that does not require battery replacement. This mechanism was adopted as Seiko's core movement and later renamed "A.G.S.". (Automatic Generating System). In 1991, to increase popularity, the watches were relaunched under the name "Seiko Kinetic".Adv. {{cite magazine |magazine=Newsweek |page=15 |date=December 18, 1995 |title=How could we fit 50 patents inside? We took out the battery}} === Recent development === [[File:Seiko 6G34-00A0 "Le Grand".jpg|thumb|Seiko Le Grand]] In 1998, Grand Seiko was released with the first new mechanical movement in 20 years. In 1999, Seiko launched [[Spring Drive]], the world's first mechanical wristwatch with the accuracy of quartz. In 2004, the Astron, launched in 1969, was selected as an [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]] milestone. In the same year, Seiko began operating the Shizukuishi Watch Studio, which specializes in high-end watches. In 2005, Seiko launched the world's first solar-powered analog watch that adjusts its accuracy by receiving three radio signals from Japan, Germany, and the United States. In 2006, Seiko launched the world's first wristwatch based on microcapsule E-ink technology. This watch was the first Seiko watch to win an award at the Grand Prix de Genève for its innovative ability to bend the display part, in addition to providing more contrast and a wider viewing angle than conventional LCDs. In 2010, Seiko launched the world's first solar radio-controlled digital watch based on the active matrix EPD system, advancing the expression of information in digital watches. [[File:Seiko Astron GPS watches.JPG|thumb|Astron GPS Solar]] In 2012, Seiko launched the world's first GPS solar watch, the Seiko Astron GPS Solar. Seiko positioned this watch as the second revolutionary wristwatch after the Astron, which was launched in 1969, and described that it had the ultimate practical functionality, being able to instantly display extremely accurate time anywhere in the world and working as long as there is light. Seiko's low power consumption GPS receiver contributed to the practical application of this watch. In April 2025, Seiko announced the Grand Seiko SLGB001 and SLGB003, the most accurate mainspring-driven watches in history. The Spring Drive Caliber 9RB2 dramatically improved the accuracy of mainspring-driven watches from the previous Spring Drive Caliber's record of ±15 seconds per month to ±20 seconds per year.{{cite web|url=https://www.hodinkee.com/articles/introducing-grand-seiko-ultra-fine-accuracy|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250403090637/https://www.hodinkee.com/articles/introducing-grand-seiko-ultra-fine-accuracy|title=Grand Seiko Achieves World-Record Mechanical Accuracy In The SLGB001 And SLGB003 – Plus Micro-Adjust Is Now Here|publisher=Hodinkee|date=31 March 2025|archive-date=3 April 2025|access-date=3 April 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.gearpatrol.com/watches/grand-seiko-spring-drive-ufa/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250403092436/https://www.gearpatrol.com/watches/grand-seiko-spring-drive-ufa/|title=Grand Seiko Just Revolutionized Watch Accuracy. Again|publisher=Gear Patrol|date=31 March 2025|archive-date=3 April 2025|access-date=3 April 2025}} {{Clear}} ==Seiko Group== {{Main|Seiko Group}} Hattori Tokeiten (K. Hattori & Co., currently Seiko Group Corporation) was one of the three principal companies of the former [[Seiko Group]]. The group was mainly composed of Hattori Tokeiten (K. Hattori), Daini Seikosha (currently [[Seiko Instruments|Seiko Instruments Inc.]], SII), and Suwa Seikosha (currently [[Seiko Epson Corporation]], Epson). Although they shared activities in the manufacturing and marketing of clocks and watches, the three companies were not formally affiliated as parent and subsidiary, nor as sibling companies under the Seiko Group; each was managed and operated independently, despite having some common shareholders, including key members of the Hattori family (posterity of Kintarō Hattori). Manufacturing was handled by three "Seikosha": [[Seikosha]], the factory division of Hattori Tokeiten (K. Hattori), and two separate companies, Daini Seikosha and Suwa Seikosha. While there were no direct capital links among the three companies, they were connected through personal networks, centered around Hattori Tokeiten (K. Hattori), which managed sales.{{cite web|url=https://riim.ws.hosei.ac.jp/wp-content/uploads/2014/10/WPNo.68_kimura.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240416173307/https://riim.ws.hosei.ac.jp/wp-content/uploads/2014/10/WPNo.68_kimura.pdf|title=セイコーエプソン・事業多角化の起源|publisher= The Research Institute for Innovation Management, [[Hosei University]]|date=|archive-date=16 April 2024|access-date=}} === Corporate evolution within the Seiko Group === In 1892, Kintarō Hattori established Seikosha in Ishiwara, Honjo Ward, [[Tokyo City]] (now [[Sumida, Tokyo]]), as the first factory of Hattori Tokeiten (K. Hattori & Co.), beginning with the production of wall clocks. The following year, the factory was relocated to Yanagishima, Honjo Ward, and in 1895 pocket watch production commenced, followed by wristwatch production in 1913.{{cite web|url=https://www.gressive.jp/special/impression/20220325-grand-seiko-shizukuishi/01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250817225354/https://www.gressive.jp/special/impression/20220325-grand-seiko-shizukuishi/01|script-title=ja:“東洋の時計王”服部金太郎が築いた時計王国「セイコー」の基盤|language=ja|publisher= Bestnavi.jp company|date=|archive-date=17 August 2025|access-date=}} In 1917, Hattori Tokeiten (K. Hattori & Co.) was incorporated with a capital of five million yen, and its English name became K. Hattori & Co., Ltd.{{cite web|url=https://www.seiko.co.jp/en/group/history/chronology.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250326082819/https://www.seiko.co.jp/en/group/history/chronology.html|title=History－Details|publisher= Seiko|date=|archive-date=26 March 2025|access-date=}} After Hattori's death, the pocket watch and wristwatch manufacturing division was spun off from K. Hattori in 1937 to establish Daini Seikosha as an independent company, and in 1939 a new factory for Daini Seikosha was completed in Kameido (now [[Kōtō, Tokyo]]). This established a division of labor in which Seikosha manufactured clocks and Daini Seikosha manufactured watches.{{cite web|url=https://www.gressive.jp/special/impression/20220325-grand-seiko-shizukuishi/02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250717011856/https://www.gressive.jp/special/impression/20220325-grand-seiko-shizukuishi/02|script-title=ja:服部時計店のウオッチ製造部門『第二精工舎』誕生|language=ja|publisher= Bestnavi.jp company|date=|archive-date=17 July 2025|access-date=}} In 1942, Hisao Yamazaki founded Daiwa Kogyo in [[Suwa, Nagano|Suwa]], [[Nagano Prefecture]], as a cooperative factory for Daini Seikosha, which produced and assembled watch components. In 1943, to avoid air raids by the U.S. military, Daini Seikosha established a wartime relocated factory near Daiwa Kogyo in Suwa. After the war, in 1959, Daini Seikosha's relocated factory was merged with Daiwa Kogyo to form Suwa Seikosha. In 1960, Suwa Seikosha developed the first Grand Seiko.{{cite web|url=https://the-shashi.com/tse/6724/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250513094203/https://the-shashi.com/tse/6724/|script-title=ja:セイコーエプソンの歴史|language=ja|publisher= Shashi.com|date=|archive-date=13 May 2025|access-date=}} In 1961, Suwa Seikosha established a subsidiary, Shinshu Seiki, for the manufacture of watch components. Ahead of the 1964 Tokyo Olympics, Seikosha focused on the development of quartz technology for time measurement, while Suwa Seikosha concentrated on printer technology to output recorded times. This allowed Suwa Seikosha to establish its own research and development system, and from around 1968 it began producing and selling printers and electronic components. Suwa Seikosha developed the Astron, the world’s first commercial quartz watch. In 1985, Suwa Seikosha merged with Shinshu Seiki, which had been renamed Epson in 1982, to become Seiko Epson. In 1970, Daini Seikosha established Morioka Seiko Kogyo (Morioka Seiko Instruments) in [[Shizukuishi, Iwate|Shizukuishi]], [[Iwate Prefecture]], as a watch manufacturing factory, which began operations in 1971. In 1974, Ninohe Tokei Kogyo was founded in [[Ninohe, Iwate|Ninohe]], Iwate Prefecture, to supply parts for Morioka Seiko Instruments. In 1983, Daini Seikosha was renamed Seiko Denshi Kogyo (Seiko Instruments & Electronics Ltd). In 1996, Tono Seiki, a watch component manufacturer, became a subsidiary. With this addition, Seiko Denshi Kogyo established an integrated watch production system in Iwate Prefecture, centered on Morioka Seiko Instruments. The company was renamed Seiko Instruments Inc. (セイコーインスツルメンツ, Seiko Insutsurumentsu) in 1997. In 2004, its Japanese name was slightly modified to セイコーインスツル (Seiko Insutsuru), while the English name remained unchanged.{{cite web|url=https://www.sii.co.jp/jp/corp/history/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250427133129/https://www.sii.co.jp/jp/corp/history/|script-title=ja:会社沿革|language=ja|publisher= Seiko Instruments|date=|archive-date=27 April 2025|access-date=}} In 1970, Seikosha, which had remained as the factory division of K. Hattori, was spun off as a separate corporation. Seikosha ceased to exist in 1996 with the establishment of Seiko Clock and Seiko Precision. In 1983, Hattori Tokeiten (K. Hattori) was renamed Hattori Seiko (Hattori Seiko Co., Ltd). In 1997, Hattori Seiko was renamed Seiko (Seiko Corporation). In 2001, Seiko Corporation became a holding company, and Seiko Watch Corporation was established to take over the watch business. In 2007, Seiko Corporation was renamed Seiko Holdings Corporation. On January 26, 2009, Seiko Holdings and Seiko Instruments announced the two companies would merge on October 1, 2009, through a share swap. Seiko Instruments became a wholly owned subsidiary of Seiko Holdings as of 1 October 2009. In 2020, the watch business of Seiko Instruments was transferred to Seiko Watch Corporation, a subsidiary of Seiko Holdings Corporation. Seiko Watch Corporation operates multiple subsidiaries engaged in the manufacture, maintenance and repair, and sales of watches. Its regional sales and distribution companies are organized separately for Seiko and Grand Seiko. For example, in the United States, Seiko Watch Corporation manages two subsidiaries: Grand Seiko Corporation of America and Seiko Watch of America LLC.{{cite web|url=https://www.seikowatches.com/jp-ja/company/global|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250401052056/https://www.seikowatches.com/jp-ja/company/global|script-title=ja:事業拠点|language=ja|publisher= Seiko Watch Corporation|date=|archive-date=1 April 2025|access-date=}} On October 1, 2022, Seiko Holdings Corporation was renamed Seiko Group Corporation. Epson still develops and manufactures some of Seiko's highest-grade watches, but is managed and operated completely independently from Seiko Group. As of March 2025, Epson's revenue is more than four times greater than that of Seiko Group Corporation, and its number of employees is over six times larger.{{cite web|url=https://corporate.epson/en/about/info.html|title=Company Outline|date=|access-date=2025-06-05}} Epson fully acquired [[Orient Watch]], originally founded in 1901, in 2009, and integrated its operations into Epson's business in 2017.{{cite web|url=https://toyokeizai.net/articles/-/136502?display=b|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250605230925/https://toyokeizai.net/articles/-/136502?display=b|title=｢時計大手｣エプソン､オリエント統合の意味|publisher=Toyo Keizai Inc.|date=September 19, 2016|archive-date=5 June 2025}} In October 2025, Tono Seiki and Ninohe Tokei Kogyo, subsidiaries of Morioka Seiko Instruments, were renamed Tono Seiko and Ninohe Seiko, respectively.{{cite web|url=https://www.morioka-seiko.co.jp/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251114042403/https://www.morioka-seiko.co.jp/|script-title=ja:関係会社2社「二戸時計工業株式会社」、「遠野精器株式会社」社名変更のお知らせ|language=ja|publisher=Morioka Seiko Instruments|date=|archive-date=14 November 2025|access-date=}} During the era of K. Hattori & Co., Ltd., the company's headquarters was located in [[Ginza]] 4-chome, at the site of the present-day [[Wako (retailer)|Seiko House Ginza]], from 1932. During the period it was known as Seiko Holdings Corporation, the headquarters was located in [[Toranomon]] until 2016, after which it moved to Ginza 1-chome. The headquarters has remained in Ginza 1-chome since the company was renamed Seiko Group Corporation.{{cite web|url=https://japan.cnet.com/article/35085390/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812172229/https://japan.cnet.com/article/35085390/|title=銀座のセイコー新社屋を訪問--エントランスに世界時計「Seiko Space Eye」|publisher=CNET Japan|date=July 9, 2016|archive-date=12 August 2024}} ===Subsidiaries=== [[File:Poor man's GS.jpg|thumb|upright|Seiko SARB035]] [[File:Pulsar Montre 4.JPG|thumb|upright|Pulsar Montre 4]] * Seiko Watch Corporation — Planning, development and manufacturing of watches and other products and domestic and overseas sales. Product planning and sales of clocks—including wall clocks, desk clocks, and alarm clocks–for both domestic and international markets{{cite web|url=https://www.seiko.co.jp/en/group/list/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251114050401/https://www.seiko.co.jp/en/group/list/|title=Affiliated Companies|publisher=Seiko Group Corporation|date=|archive-date=14 November 2025}} * [[Seiko Instruments|Seiko Instruments Inc.]] — Development, manufacturing and sales of electronic components, precision components and printing devices * Seiko Solutions Inc. — Development, manufacturing, sales, maintenance, services and consultations for the hardware and the software relating with information systems and network services * Seiko Time Creation Inc. — Development, manufacturing, and sales of facility clocks, sports timing systems, digital signage, and large-scale display boards, including related installation services and timekeeping support for sporting events * [[Wako (retailer)|Wako Co., Ltd.]] — Sales of watches, jewelry, accessories, interior supplies, art goods and crafts, glasses and foodstuffs * Seiko NPC Corporation — Design, development, manufacturing, and sales of semiconductor products * Seiko Future Creation Inc. — Group-wide R&D and production technology development, plus provision of FA systems and Provision of analytical instrumentation and microfabrication services ===Manufacturing sites=== Seiko watches and their components are manufactured in Japan and several other countries in Asia. Morioka Seiko Instruments is a subsidiary of Seiko Watch Corporation, while Tono Seiko and Ninohe Seiko are subsidiaries of Morioka Seiko Instruments.{{cite web|url=https://www.seiko.co.jp/news/holdings/2022/202206151400.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250722112823/https://www.seiko.co.jp/news/holdings/2022/202206151400.html|script-title=ja:国内腕時計３工場で、使用電力を100％再生可能エネルギー化|language=ja|publisher=Seiko|date=|archive-date=22 Seiko has manufacturing facilities for watch parts and movements in Singapore, Malaysia, and China. In the late 1990s, the company transferred half of its movement production to a subsidiary in Singapore. Since the late 2010s, certain plastic component molding processes have been consolidated in China, while some metal processing operations have been consolidated in Malaysia.{{cite web|url=https://meiji.repo.nii.ac.jp/record/17537/files/seikeironso_91_3-4_1.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250706210013/https://meiji.repo.nii.ac.jp/record/17537/files/seikeironso_91_3-4_1.pdf|title=日本の時計製造産地におけるサプライヤーの再編|pages=12, 13|publisher=[[Meiji University]]|archive-date=6 July 2025|access-date=5 August 2025}} In 2020, these overseas manufacturing operations were reorganized as subsidiaries under Seiko Watch Corporation.{{cite web|url=https://www.edb.gov.sg/ja/industries-case-studies/case-studies-library/seiko.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250805053951/https://www.edb.gov.sg/ja/industries-case-studies/case-studies-library/seiko.html|title=セイコー・マニュファクチャリング・シンガポール|publisher=Singapore Economic Development Board|archive-date=5 August 2025|access-date=5 August 2025}} == Brands and product lines == Seiko produces watches with [[Quartz clock|quartz]], [[Automatic quartz|kinetic]], [[Solar-powered watch|solar]], [[Mechanical watch|mechanical]], and [[Spring Drive]] movements of varying prices, ranging from around ¥4,000 (US$45) to ¥50,000,000 (US$554,000). Seiko has created many brands in Japan and the international market including Lorus, [[Pulsar (watch)|Pulsar]], and [[Alba (watch)|Alba]]. In 2015, the ''[[Financial Times]]'' reported that the enthusiastic reception of the [[Spring Drive]] movement prompted Seiko to launch higher-end pieces. Harvard Business School reported: "In 2003, Shinji Hattori, a great-grandson of Seiko's founder, became Seiko Watch Company's president and CEO and felt that Seiko should raise its perceived image outside Japan. In management's view, Seiko could claim distinction as the only 'mechatronic manufacturer' in the world – a vertically integrated watchmaker that excelled in both mechanical watchmaking and micro-electronics."Hoosain, A., Ho, M., Farhoomand, A. and Hout, T., 2007. Seiko Watch Corporation: Moving Upmarket ^ HKU658. [online] Harvard Business Review. Available at: [Accessed 18 January 2022]. In 2017 and 2019, Seiko separated its two highest-end brands, Grand Seiko and Credor, from its other brand lines, establishing them as independent brands with their own operations and distribution networks.{{cite web|url=https://deployant.com/baselworld-2017-history-grand-seiko-independence/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250124075038/https://deployant.com/baselworld-2017-history-grand-seiko-independence/|title=Baselworld 2017 Grand Seiko declares Independence|publisher=Deployant|date=March 24, 2017|archive-date=24 January 2025}} As of 2025, Seiko positions Grand Seiko, King Seiko, Seiko Prospex, Seiko Astron, Seiko Presage, and Seiko 5 Sports as global brands with worldwide distribution.{{cite web|url=https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/8050/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/178496/00.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250603192632/https://ssl4.eir-parts.net/doc/8050/ir_material_for_fiscal_ym2/178496/00.pdf|title=2025年3月期 通期 決算説明会|publisher=Seiko Group Corporation|date=|archive-date=3 June 2025}} In contrast, some brands such as Credor are marketed primarily in specific countries, such as Japan. === Seiko 5 === [[File:Seiko-5-blue-gold.jpg|thumb|210x210px|A Seiko 5 showcasing attributes of the sub brand, including a recessed crown at the 4 o'clock position and day-date complication]] Seiko 5 is a [[Brand#Subbranding|sub brand]] that spawned with the introduction of the Seiko Sportsmatic 5 in 1963. Since then, many models have been introduced into the lineup, comprising a variety of styles. The name of the Seiko 5 sub brand is a reference to five attributes that any watch belonging to it would typically exhibit: # An automatic watch movement # The day and the date displayed on the dial # Water resistance to an acceptable degree # A recessed crown at the 4 o'clock position # A durable case and bracelet{{Cite web |title=Seiko 5, The People's Watch |url=https://montrespubliques.com/1minute-reads/seiko5 |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=Montres Publiques |date=September 21, 2019 |language=en-CA}}{{Cite web|title=About – Seiko 5 Sports |url=https://www.seikowatches.com/us-en/products/5sports/about|access-date=2021-12-06|website=www.seikowatches.com|language=en}} In spite of their association with the brand, not all of these characteristics are universal across the lineup, as certain models have omitted the Day-Date display (such as the SSA333) and/or the 4 o'clock positioning of the crown (such as the SRPG31K1 and the aforementioned SSA333). Seiko released many models under the Seiko 5 sub brand, including large and small divers; watches featuring different strap options, such as leather, nylon, or steel; transparent, or sterile case-back versions; and many other variations. === Seiko Lord Matic === Seiko Lord Matic line of watches was introduced in 1968 and became popular in the 1970s.{{cite web |url=https://www.beyondthedial.com/post/birth-year-seiko-watches-1970-79/ |title=Collector Guide. Birth-Year Seiko Watches: 1970–1979 |author=David Flett |date=June 19, 2020 |publisher=Beyond the dial |access-date=July 13, 2025}} It featured design innovations such as faceted crystals, colorful dials and sporty bracelets. === Seiko Astron === The Seiko Astron series is a quartz watch which receives time information and location information from [[Global Positioning System|GPS satellites]].{{Cite web |title=Astron |url=https://www.seikowatches.com/us-en/products/astron |access-date=2024-07-31 |website=Seiko Watch Corporation |language=en-US}} These watches also have a [[solar panel]] which means that the battery does not need to be replaced. === Seiko Presage === The Seiko Presage series is an all-mechanical lineup, a step up from the entry-level Seiko 5 models. It has slightly more elaborate designs and complex movements, such as urushi-lacquer dials, and self-winding movements with power reserve indicators.{{Cite web|url=https://www.hodinkee.com/articles/the-seiko-presage-automatic-60th-anniversary-limited-edition-sarw027|title=Introducing: The Seiko Presage Automatic 60th Anniversary Limited Edition, SARW027|date=December 8, 2016|first=Jack|last=Forster|website=Hodinkee|language=en|access-date=2019-12-12}} The Presage line watches are usually priced between US$200 to US$3,000.{{Cite web|url=https://automaticwatchesformen.com/what-is-the-history-of-seiko|title=What Is The History Of Seiko? |website=Automatic Watches For Men|language=en-US|access-date=2019-12-12}} Seiko entered a cooperation with the traditional [[cloisonné]] maker [[Ando Cloisonné Company]] from [[Nagoya]] to produce the dial for the limited edition in 2018.{{Cite web|title=The Shippo Enamel Limited Edition |url=https://www.seikowatches.com/us-en/products/presage/special/shippoenamel/|access-date=2020-10-14|website=The Shippo Enamel Limited Edition |language=en}}{{Cite web|title=Baselworld 2018 Releases – Seiko Presage|url=https://www.plus9time.com/blog/2018/3/22/baselworld-2018-seiko-presage|access-date=2020-10-14|website=Plus9Time|date=March 22, 2018 |language=en-US}} === Seiko Prospex === [[File:Seiko Prospex SPB143J1.png|alt=Seiko SPB143J1|thumb|270x270px|Seiko Prospex SPB143J ]] The Seiko Prospex series includes their professional series of watches such as their [[diving watch]]es, which are typically [[diving watches#ISO 6425 divers' watches standard|ISO 6425]] rated from 200 to 1000 metres of water resistance. Other watches in the Prospex line include field and pilot style watches. In 2021, Akio Naito, President of the Seiko Watch Corporation,{{Cite news |date=2021-10-01 |title=Akio Naito: Seiko watches have to go back to their roots to grow again |work=Financial Times |url=https://www.ft.com/content/eabf51ad-4f94-4c99-a873-068451fc75f4 |access-date=2023-04-06}} said that enthusiasts' respect for the brand can "influence the wider range of consumers."{{Cite web |last=Soman |first=Ashok |date=2021-09-24 |title=Seiko President Akio Naito on Making the Sports Watch Work for Grand Seiko |url=https://www.luxuo.com/leaders/watches-leaders/seiko-president-akio-naito.html |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=Luxuo |language=en-US}} This influence can be seen in the Prospex range, where Seiko fans' nicknames resulted in the company eventually adopting these product names. For example, Seiko's own London boutique identifies the Prospex SPB191J1 watch using the fans' sobriquet: "Nicknamed 'Shogun' by fans, meaning Japanese 'Commander-in-chief', because of its strong looks."Seikoboutique.co.uk. 2021. Prospex 'Shogun' | Seiko Boutique. [online] Available at: [Accessed 12 January 2022]. In 2025, Seiko announced a boutique exclusive watch, Seiko Prospex 1968 Heritage Diver GMT. The latest “Seashadow” Black Boutique Edition (SPB534) is a 500-piece limited run, exclusive to select boutiques like Seiko Bond Street, London.{{Cite web |date=October 8, 2025 |title=Seiko Prospex 1968 Heritage Diver GMT – Exclusive to Europe |url=https://tickingtales.com/seiko-prospex-1968-heritage-diver-gmt-exclusive-to-europe/ |access-date=16 October 2025 |website=TickingTales}} === Grand Seiko === {{Main|Grand Seiko}} Prior to 1960, to challenge the status of [[Swiss watch]]es and change the perception of Japanese watches, Daini [[Seikosha]] and Suwa began the discussion of a product line that could match the quality of Swiss watches under the suggestion of the [[parent company]]. At the time, Suwa Seikosha Co. was in charge of manufacturing men's watches, so it was decided that Suwa would produce the first Grand Seiko. The first Grand Seiko, released in 1960, was based on Seiko's previous high-end watch, ''CROWN''. This Grand Seiko has a 25-[[jewel (watch)|jewel]], [[manual-winding]], 3180 [[caliber (watch)|caliber]], and its production was limited to 36,000 units. The watch was also the first chronometer-grade watch manufactured in Japan and was based on Seiko's own chronometer standard.{{Cite web|url=http://www.seiyajapan.com/pages/the-history-of-grand-seiko|title=The History of Grand Seiko|website=seiyajapan.com|access-date=2016-12-02}}{{Cite web |title=History |url=https://www.grand-seiko.com/uk-en/worldofgrandseiko/historyandwatchmaking/history |access-date=2024-07-01 |website=Grand Seiko |language=en-GB}} Some Grand Seiko timepieces also incorporate the company's [[Spring Drive]] movement, a movement that is a combination of both automatic and quartz timekeeping methods, leading to unparalleled accuracy in the world of automatic wristwatches. The most famous example is the SBGA011 Grand Seiko "Snowflake", housing the 9R Spring Drive movement. Grand Seiko began expanding overseas in 2010.{{cite web|url=https://aplussingapore.com/article/grand-seiko-yoshikatsu-kawada-interview|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240228093330/https://aplussingapore.com/article/grand-seiko-yoshikatsu-kawada-interview|title=Grand Seiko's Leap Out Of Japan|publisher= a+ Singapore|date=26 May 2023|archive-date=28 February 2024}} With the repositioning of Grand Seiko from a Seiko subbrand to an independent brand in 2017, Grand Seiko aimed to transition to a true luxury brand. The transition to an independent brand accelerated this expansion, and its overseas sales grew about fifteenfold between 2015 and 2025.{{cite web|url=https://oracleoftime.com/the-worlds-of-seiko-grand-seiko-and-credor-with-president-akio-naito/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260608215329/https://oracleoftime.com/the-worlds-of-seiko-grand-seiko-and-credor-with-president-akio-naito/|title=The Worlds of Seiko, Grand Seiko and Credor with President Akio Naito|publisher= Oracle Time|date=5 June 2026|archive-date=8 June 2026}} In 2022, Kodo Constant-Force Tourbillon SLGT 003, featuring the world's first combination tourbillon and constant-force mechanism on the same axis, was released, priced at 370,000 euros.{{cite web|url=https://monochrome-watches.com/introducing-grand-seiko-kodo-constant-force-tourbillon-slgt003-specs-price/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220403093016/https://monochrome-watches.com/introducing-grand-seiko-kodo-constant-force-tourbillon-slgt003-specs-price/|title=The Grand Seiko Kodo Constant-Force Tourbillon SLGT003|publisher=MONOCHROME|date=31 March 2022|archive-date=3 April 2022}} As of 2025, Grand Seiko is guided by the brand philosophy "The Nature of Time" and is composed of five collections: the Masterpiece Collection, Evolution 9 Collection, Elegance Collection, Heritage Collection, and Sport Collection. The Masterpiece Collection is produced in special workshops staffed by Seiko's most elite watchmakers. The mechanical models are crafted at Atelier Ginza, located on the 7th floor of [[Wako (retailer)|Seiko House Ginza]] in Tokyo, while the Spring Drive models are manufactured at the Micro Artist Studio within Seiko [[Epson]]'s facility in [[Shiojiri, Nagano]].{{cite web|url=https://www.grand-seiko.com/us-en/collections/masterpiece|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250515031943/https://www.grand-seiko.com/us-en/collections/masterpiece|title=Masterpiece Collection|publisher=Seiko|date=|archive-date=15 May 2025}} The Micro Artist Studio has also been responsible for creating Credor's complicated timepieces since 2000. At Seiko House Ginza, customers can place custom orders for one-of-a-kind Grand Seiko timepieces, provided they meet certain conditions such as a high budget and the use of precious metals.{{cite web|url=https://timeandtidewatches.com/grand-seiko-manufacture-tour-part-3-the-seiko-house-ginza-wako-main-building/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250429223457/https://timeandtidewatches.com/grand-seiko-manufacture-tour-part-3-the-seiko-house-ginza-wako-main-building/|title=Grand Seiko Manufacture Tour Part 3: The Seiko House Ginza (Wako Main Building)|publisher=Time and Tide Watches|date=August 6, 2023|archive-date=29 April 2025}} ==== Design style ==== [[File:Grand Seiko.JPG|thumb|upright|Grand Seiko SBGW231]] The design language of the Grand Seiko was set in 1967, with the creation of Grand Seiko 44GS. The 44GS set the ground for all future Grand Seiko with nine elements. These elements help improve the legibility of the watch under different situations, and create a sharp, crisp visual impression:{{Cite web |title=Design {{!}} About {{!}} Grand Seiko |url=https://www.grand-seiko.com/us-en/about/design |access-date=2017-12-12 |website=www.grand-seiko.com}} # Double width index at 12 o'clock # Multi-faceted rectangular markers # Highly polished bezel # Highly polished planes and two-dimensional surface # Half recessed crown # Flat dial # Multi-faceted hour and minute hands # Curved side line # Reverse slanted bezel wall and case side # Dress style with simple but beautiful design # Zaratsu polishing === King Seiko === The King Seiko line was created by Daini Seikosha to compete directly with Grand Seiko. The first King Seiko was released the year after the first Grand Seiko, in 1961. The first King Seikos were made with unmarked, manual winding, 25 jewel movements, that were not internally tested chronometers. This was followed by the release of the '44KS' movement in 1964, a remake of the 44GS, a manual winding, 18,000 bph, movement with a screwdown case back. In 1968, the 45KS was introduced with a manual winding, 36,000 bph hi-beat movement – again meant to compete with the 45GS but generally less accurate and with less finishing. King Seiko Certified Chronometer and Superior Certified Chronometers were released between 1968 and 1970. These first two were produced by Daini Seikosha but one of the most impressive King Seikos, the 56KS, was actually made by the Suwa Seikosha. The King Seiko 56KS movements were the same as those used in Grand Seiko’s 56GS series, Seiko Lord Matic watches, and Seiko chronometers. It was also introduced in 1968 and featured an automatic, 28,800 bph movement with 25 jewels and a 47-hour power reserve. These watches were all marked ‘[[Grand Seiko Hi-Beat|Hi-Beat]]’ on the dial despite being only 28,800 bph (instead of 36,000). The 56KS was made until 1975, when the King Seiko line was discontinued by the company. The last King Seiko collection was made by Daini, and was the 52KS, starting off in 1971 and made until 1975. This line used the 5245 and 5246 movement. These were meant to be high-end chronometers, with some even marked ‘V. F. A.’ (Very Fine Accuracy) or ‘Special’ on the dial. Many of these were of the "Vanac" sub-line and featured colorful dial faces and faceted crystals.{{Cite web |title=Lord Marvel and King Seiko History |url=https://montrespubliques.com/1minute-reads/lord-marvel-and-king-seiko-history |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=Montres Publiques |date=August 4, 2020 |language=en-CA}} In 2021, Seiko released a reissue model inspired by the design of the second-generation King Seiko KSK, originally introduced in 1965, and in 2022, the company fully revived the King Seiko brand.{{cite web|url=https://www.seikowatches.com/jp-ja/products/kingseiko/ksk_webchronos|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241213051646/https://www.seikowatches.com/jp-ja/products/kingseiko/ksk_webchronos|script-title=ja:キングセイコーから新生KSK誕生。現代人の感性を刺激する、時代を超えた造形|language=ja|publisher=Seiko|date=|archive-date=13 December 2024|access-date=21 April 2025}} In the summer of 2025, Seiko plans to bring back the 1972 King Seiko VANAC using modern technology. The watch will be powered by the Caliber 8L45, which offers an accuracy of +10 to -5 seconds per day and a power reserve of 72 hours. Seiko claims that this caliber represents the highest-grade mechanical movement within the Seiko brand (excluding calibers used in the independent Grand Seiko and Credor lines).{{Cite web |last=Daniel Razvan |date=23 June 2026 |title=King Seiko VANAC – 70’s Glamour from Japan |url=https://tickingtales.com/king-seiko-vanac-70s-glamour-from-japan/ |access-date=23 June 2026 |website=TickingTales}} ===Credor=== Credor is Seiko's highest-end brand alongside Grand Seiko. Seiko positions Grand Seiko as watches for everyday use, while Credor is intended for special occasions.{{cite web|url=https://forbesjapan.com/articles/detail/36779?id=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250420224731/https://forbesjapan.com/articles/detail/36779?id=|script-title=ja:美しくあれ！ 時を豊かにするためにクレドールは進化する|language=ja|publisher=Forbes Japan|date=30 November 2020|archive-date=20 April 2025|access-date=20 April 2025}} The brand name is derived from the French words Crête d'Or, meaning "Crest (or Pinnacle) of Gold." Its logo symbolizes the peak of a mountain.{{cite web|url=https://forbesjapan.com/articles/detail/33311?id=2-1|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250420223928/https://forbesjapan.com/articles/detail/33311?id=2-1|script-title=ja:ブランドイメージを視覚化せよ！ クレドールのロゴマーク誕生秘話から読み解く「ジャパンメイドの矜持」|language=ja|publisher=Forbes Japan|date=1 July 2020|archive-date=20 April 2025|access-date=20 April 2025}} As of 2026, the brand philosophy is "The Creativity of Artisans".{{cite web|url=https://www.europastar.com/the-watch-files/watchmaking-in-japan/1004115875-credor-goes-global.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260326100102/https://www.europastar.com/the-watch-files/watchmaking-in-japan/1004115875-credor-goes-global.html|title=Credor goes global|publisher=Europa Star|date=|archive-date=26 March 2026|access-date=26 March 2026}} Credor was established in 1974 as a low-volume production line specializing in watches made with precious metals such as gold and platinum. In 2019, it was reorganized as an independent brand, like Grand Seiko, separate from Seiko's main lineup.{{cite web|url=https://www.webchronos.net/features/43886/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241008182212/https://www.webchronos.net/features/43886/|script-title=ja:グランドセイコーとクレドールって違うの? モデルから見るそれぞれの特徴|language=ja|publisher=web Chronos|date=8 May 2024|archive-date=8 October 2024|access-date=20 April 2025}} As of 2022, Credor remains primarily a domestic (Japanese) brand with limited international distribution.{{cite web|url=https://www.webchronos.net/features/84010/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241212134908/https://www.webchronos.net/features/84010/|script-title=ja:グランドセイコー・ヨーロッパ社長が考える、欧州展開のポテンシャル|language=ja|publisher=web Chronos|date=23 August 2022|archive-date=12 December 2024|access-date=20 April 2025}} Between 2021 and 2022, Seiko determined that Credor's product range and distribution network had become excessively broad and risked undermining its brand identity, and it subsequently revised its marketing with a more carefully selected lineup. In 2026, Credor exhibited at [[Watches and Wonders]] for the first time, marking its debut at an international trade fair as it seeks to expand its presence overseas. As of May 2026, there is a notable difference in the brand's lineup between Japan and international markets: the official Japanese website lists 77 models,{{cite web|url=https://www.credor.com/lineup/all/|title=All Models|language=ja|publisher=Credor|date=|access-date=3 May 2026}} whereas the English-language global website lists only 15.{{cite web|url=https://www.credor.com/en/lineup/all/|title=All Models|publisher=Credor|date=|access-date=3 May 2026}} Credor depends more on hand craftsmanship than Grand Seiko, making it more difficult to increase production. During [[Japanese asset price bubble|Japan's economic bubble]] in the late 1980s and early 1990s, high-end jeweled watches priced over 10 million yen sold well, and Credor's jeweled watches experienced a golden era.{{cite web|url=https://forbesjapan.com/articles/detail/35106?id=4-2|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250420225506/https://forbesjapan.com/articles/detail/35106?id=4-2|script-title=ja:勝負の鍵はジュエリーウォッチ！ 時計大国に挑むクレドールの初志は「日本ならではの美」だった|language=ja|publisher=Forbes Japan|date=30 July 2020|archive-date=20 April 2025|access-date=20 April 2025}} In the mid-1980s, Credor's sales in the Japanese domestic market were approximately ten times those of Grand Seiko. Since the 1990s, in addition to quartz jeweled watches, Seiko began incorporating mechanical watches into the Credor line, featuring intricate engravings based on traditional Japanese aesthetics. In 1996, the brand released its first [[skeleton watch]], the GBBD998, which featured the ultra-thin 1.98 mm Caliber 6899 and a caliber engraved with motifs of swaying bamboo and chrysanthemums.{{cite web|url=https://forbesjapan.com/articles/detail/35806?id=1-4|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250420225811/https://forbesjapan.com/articles/detail/35806?id=1-4|script-title=ja:どこまでも薄く、美しく! 熱い想いで連綿と受け継がれてきた「透ける時計」、スケルトンウォッチ|language=ja|publisher=Forbes Japan|date=30 July 2020|archive-date=20 April 2025|access-date=20 April 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.seikowatches.com/jp-ja/news/20210624|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116104412/https://www.seikowatches.com/jp-ja/news/20210624|script-title=ja:＜クレドール＞スケルトンモデルの誕生25周年を記念して、ハンドワークの粋を極めた「Art Piece Collection」の最高峰モデルが登場|language=ja|publisher=Seiko|date=23 June 2021|archive-date=16 November 2023|access-date=20 April 2025}} In 2000, Seiko established the Micro Artist Studio at [[Epson]]'s facility in [[Shiojiri, Nagano]], to begin producing [[Complication (horology)|haute horlogerie]], which refers to high-end, artisanal Spring Drive watches, under the Credor name. Notable creations by the studio include the Credor Node Spring Drive [[Sonnerie]] (2006), Credor Node Eichi (2008), Credor Node Spring Drive [[Repeater (horology)|Minute Repeater]] (2011), and Credor Eichi II (2014). Because Seiko had largely lost its capacity for high-end mechanical watchmaking by the late 1990s due to the quartz revolution, the release of the Spring Drive Sonnerie only six years after the studio's founding surprised many watch journalists.{{cite web|url=https://www.webchronos.net/iconic/39405/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241114185030/https://www.webchronos.net/iconic/39405/|script-title=ja:クレドール／マイクロアーティスト工房編|language=ja|publisher=web Chronos|date=21 June 2024|archive-date=14 November 2024|access-date=20 April 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.credor.com/about/history/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250401155240/https://web.archive.org/web/20250401155240/https://www.credor.com/about/history/|title=History|language=ja|publisher=Seiko|date=|archive-date=April 1, 2025|access-date=20 April 2025|url-status=bot: unknown}} Credor is also known for its artistic watches decorated with traditional [[Japanese lacquerware|Japanese lacquer]] techniques such as ''[[maki-e]]'', ''[[raden]]'', ''kirikane'' (gold leaf cutting), and ''zōgan'' (metal inlay). In 1987, Credor released its first [[pocket watch]] featuring lacquer decoration. In 2016, the brand launched the Fugaku [[Tourbillon]], the first Seiko watch with a tourbillon, priced at 50 million yen, featuring a dial adorned with [[Hokusai]]'s ''[[The Great Wave off Kanagawa]]'' rendered in engraving and lacquer art.{{cite web|url=https://forbesjapan.com/articles/detail/36933?id=1-6|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250420231108/https://forbesjapan.com/articles/detail/36933?id=1-6|script-title=ja:伝統工芸で活路を開く！独自の世界観を確立した「職人の至芸」|language=ja|publisher=Forbes Japan|date=10 November 2020|archive-date=20 April 2025|access-date=20 April 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.hodinkee.com/articles/the-seiko-fugaku-limited-edition-tourbillon|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221226003644/https://www.hodinkee.com/articles/the-seiko-fugaku-limited-edition-tourbillon|title=The Seiko FUGAKU Limited Edition Tourbillon|publisher=Hodinkee|date=7 April 2016|archive-date=26 December 2022|access-date=20 April 2025}} In 2025, Credor released a new Goldfeather Tourbillon priced at 25.3 million yen, featuring a newly developed caliber that succeeds the one used in the Fugaku. The watch is adorned with engravings and urushi lacquer art depicting birds and feathers.{{cite web|url=https://deployant.com/new-credor-goldfeather-tourbillon-with-urushi-lacquer-techniques/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250725161024/https://deployant.com/new-credor-goldfeather-tourbillon-with-urushi-lacquer-techniques/|title=Credor Goldfeather Tourbillon with urushi lacquer techniques|publisher=Deployant|date=24 July 2025|archive-date=25 July 2025|access-date=3 August 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.credor.com/en/news/press_release/20250724/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250724070902/https://www.credor.com/en/news/press_release/20250724/|title=Credor soars with the masterful expression of diverse urushi lacquer techniques in a new Goldfeather tourbillon.|publisher=Seiko Watch Corporation|date=24 July 2025|archive-date=24 July 2025|access-date=3 August 2025}} === TimeTron === In the late 1990s, Seiko introduced, Seiko TimeTron, a line of digital watches with [[Retrofuturism|retrofuturistic]] design aimed at the young audience. It had an unconventional PC-inspired appearance, a [[dot-matrix display]] (and a button to change the size of the characters), was produced in a variety of colors for the case and the strap. Several models of TimeTron have been produced in limited numbers compared to other Seiko lines.{{cite web |url=https://90kids.com/seiko-timetron-a-retro-futuristic-gem-that-still-captures-hearts/ |title=Seiko TimeTron: A Retro-Futuristic Gem That Still Captures Hearts |work=90kids.com – Childhood Nostalgia |date=May 14, 2025 |publisher=90kids |access-date=July 13, 2025}}{{cite web |url=https://www.yankodesign.com/2024/12/04/designer-introduces-iconic-seiko-h-timetron-watch-in-3d-to-the-gen-z/ |title=Designer introduces iconic Seiko H-Timetron watch in 3D to the Gen-Z |author=Gaurav Sood |date=April 12, 2024 |publisher=Yanko Design |access-date=July 13, 2025}} === Other === Seiko produces electronic devices as well; during the 1980s, the company produced a notable range of [[digital synthesizer]]s, such as the DS-202 and [[Seiko DS-250|DS-250]], for use in electronic music. Today the music division (part of Seiko Instruments Inc.) produces metronomes and tuning devices.{{cite web |title=Metronomes |url=https://www.sii.co.jp/music/english/ |website=Seiko Instruments Inc. |access-date=2 June 2024}} Seiko was previously engaged in the manufacturing and sale of jewelry, but exited the business in 2008.{{cite web|url=https://www.seiko.co.jp/upload_files/ir2007_1009a.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250606002836/https://www.seiko.co.jp/upload_files/ir2007_1009a.pdf|script-title=ja:連結子会社の解散に関するお知らせ|language=ja|publisher=Seiko|date=|archive-date=6 June 2025|access-date=6 June 2025}} The company also sold its eyewear business to [[Hoya Corporation]] in 2014. However, eyewear products under the Seiko brand have continued to be sold by Hoya.{{cite web|url=https://www.hoya.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/15.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230802224016/https://www.hoya.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/15.pdf|title=Hoya Report 2015|language=ja|publisher=Hoya Corporation|date=|archive-date=2 August 2023|access-date=6 June 2025}} In addition, Wako has continued to sell jewelry and eyewear from companies other than Seiko. == Movements == === Mechanical movement === [[File:Seiko SNK381 with 7S26-01V0.jpg|thumb|Seiko SNK381 with 7S26-01V0 movement]] Seiko developed the Caliber 60, which at the time was the world’s thinnest center-seconds movement at 2.95 mm, and in 1960 released the Seiko Goldfeather, a slim dress watch housing this caliber. The origin of the still-ongoing Caliber 68 series lies in the Caliber 6800, which measured just 1.98 mm in thickness and was first used in the Seiko U.T.D., released in 1969. After a period of discontinuation, the 68 series was revived in the 1990s, and as of the 2020s, updated versions such as the Caliber 6890 continue to be produced for ultra-thin dress watches, including Credor's Goldfeather line.{{cite web|url=https://www.webchronos.net/features/125547/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250117115635/https://www.webchronos.net/features/125547/|script-title=ja:セイコー クレドール「Cal.68系」。未来に残したい時計遺産【傑作ムーブメント列伝】|language=ja|publisher=webChronos|date=8 December 2024|archive-date=17 January 2025|access-date=26 April 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.webchronos.net/features/96984/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241111015955/https://www.webchronos.net/features/96984/|script-title=ja:クレドール ゴールドフェザー その薄さ、羽根の如く。～|language=ja|publisher=webChronos|date=6 June 2023|archive-date=11 November 2024|access-date=26 April 2025}} In 1968, Seiko introduced three ten beat (ten ticks per second) calibers, the automatic caliber 61GS, the manual winding 45GS{{Cite web|url=https://www.strapcode.com/pages/what-is-the-difference-between-seiko-and-grand-seiko/|title=Grand Seiko GS 45GS V.F.A.|website=strapcode.com|access-date=2020-10-07}} and 19GS{{Cite web|url=https://www.strapcode.com/pages/grand-seiko-movements-3-driving-system-quartz-mechanical-spring-driver/|title=Grand Seiko for Women 19GS|website=strapcode.com|access-date=2020-10-07}} for women's watch. The 61GS was Japan's first [[automatic movement|automatic]] ten beat watch, and it was the most accurate mechanical watch due to the high beat calibers.{{Cite web|url=http://www.grand-seiko.com/movement/mechanical.php#tabContent01|title=Grand Seiko |website=www.grand-seiko.com|access-date=2016-12-02}} The calibers are considered high beat because normal [[mechanical movement]]s beat six to eight times per second, and higher beat makes the watch more resistant to shock, thus achieving the high accuracy.{{Cite web|url=https://www.strapcode.com/pages/grand-seiko-9s-movement-the-new-generation-of-mechanical-calibers|title=Grand Seiko Hi Beat Caliber 9S85|website=strapcode.com|access-date=2020-10-07}} Seiko developed the Caliber 6139, featuring a Magic Lever, column wheel, and a groundbreaking vertical clutch mechanism, and in 1969 released the Seiko 5 Sports Speed Timer, the world’s first commercially available automatic chronograph. The vertical clutch system, used to transmit power for the start and stop functions of the stopwatch, had a significant impact on the subsequent development of chronographs worldwide. In 2009, Seiko released the new ten beat caliber 9S85,{{Cite web|title=Grand Seiko Caliber 9S85|url=http://calibercorner.com/grand-seiko-caliber-9s85/|access-date=2016-12-02|website=calibercorner.com|date=December 21, 2014 }} which is a completely new design from the previous high beat caliber. The new caliber also met the Grand Seiko Standard, a chronometer certification that the company claims to be more strict than the [[COSC|Chronometer Certificate]] in Switzerland.{{Cite web|url=http://www.grand-seiko.com/movement/mechanical.php#tabContent03|title=Grand Seiko |website=www.grand-seiko.com|access-date=2016-12-02}}{{Cite web |title=The Grand Seiko Standard Inspection Certificate |url=https://www.grand-seiko.com/instructions/html/GS_9SA4_en/AGFISYfijesakn |access-date=2024-07-01 |website=www.grand-seiko.com}} Seiko developed the Caliber 6830 and, in 2016, released the Credor Fugaku, its first watch featuring a [[tourbillon]], priced at 50 million yen.{{cite web|url=https://www.seikowatches.com/jp-ja/news/20160317_02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241113024956/https://www.seikowatches.com/jp-ja/news/20160317_02|script-title=ja:高級ウオッチブランド＜クレドール＞より、 新開発ムーブメントに独自の立体彫金と高度な漆芸の技を融合させた セイコー初のトゥールビヨンモデル「FUGAKU」を発売 ～世界的に評価の高い名作浮世絵「富嶽三十六景」からインスピレーション～|language=ja|publisher=Seiko|date=17 March 2016|archive-date=13 November 2024|access-date=21 April 2025}} The company later developed the Caliber 9ST1 and, in 2022, launched the Grand Seiko Kodo, the world's first timepiece to integrate both a tourbillon and a constant-force mechanism on a single axis, priced at 44 million yen.{{cite web|url=https://www.webchronos.net/news/78165/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241107123459/https://www.webchronos.net/news/78165/|script-title=ja:【2022年 新作】世界初の機構を備えたグランドセイコーの傑作「Kodo（鼓動）コンスタントフォース・トゥールビヨン」誕生|language=ja|publisher=webChronos|date=8 April 2022|archive-date=7 November 2024|access-date=21 April 2025}} In 2025, Seiko announced the Caliber 6850 as the successor to the Caliber 6830, increasing the power reserve from 37 to 60 hours. The new movement was introduced in the Goldfeather Tourbillon, released under the Credor brand at a price of 25.3 million yen. Seiko developed the innovative Dual Impulse Escapement and introduced it in 2020 with the Caliber 9SA5. This escapement is the second non-[[lever escapement]] to be produced on an industrial scale, following [[George Daniels (watchmaker)|George Daniels]]' Co-Axial escapement, which is used in [[Omega SA|Omega]] watches. Inv. {{not a typo|2010-006}})]] On 25 December 1969, Seiko released the world's first [[Quartz clock|quartz]] watch, the [[Astron (wristwatch)|Seiko Quartz ASTRON]], marking the beginning of the [[quartz revolution]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.hodinkee.com/articles/four-revolutions-quartz-revolution|title=Four Revolutions: Part 1: A Concise History Of The Quartz Revolution|date=October 10, 2017|first=Joe|last=Thompson|website=Hodinkee|language=en|access-date=2019-03-05}}{{Cite web |title=The Story of 1969 Quartz Astron and GPS solar Astron |url=https://www.seikowatches.com/global-en/products/astron/special/story_qa50th_1/ |access-date=2024-07-01 |website=The Story of 1969 Quartz Astron and GPS solar Astron |language=en}}{{Cite web|url=https://blog.crownandcaliber.com/the-quartz-crisis/|title=The Quartz Crisis|date=2018-04-12|website=Crown & Caliber Blog|language=en-US|access-date=2019-03-05}} The watch used a [[crystal oscillator]] for accuracy, where the crystal generates steady vibration when voltage is applied to it. During the ten years of development at Suwa Seikosha, Seiko managed to create many parts which enabled the viable application of quartz in wristwatches. For example, Seiko cut the crystal oscillator into the shape of a [[Tuning fork|tuning-fork]], and developed an [[integrated circuit]] and step motor to operate with the signals from the crystal oscillator. Although creating the parts that enabled quartz watches, Seiko did not monopolize the patent rights for the unique pieces, but decided to open them. In 1973, Seiko announced the world's first LCD quartz watch with six-digit digital display. In 1975, Seiko launched the world's first multi-function digital watch, the 0634. In 1978, Seiko released the Twin Quartz watch to address the effect of temperature on the frequency of the quartz crystal oscillator, which put a limitation on the accuracy of quartz watches. Seiko put a second crystal in the watch that is linked with a processor that detects the change in temperature and signals the main oscillator to compensate. The result was a huge improvement in the watch's accuracy from five seconds per month to five seconds per year. Kinetic watches were introduced by Seiko in 1986 at the Basel Fair Trade Show.{{cite web|title=About Seiko Kinetic watches and Kinetic Movements|url=https://www.strapcode.com/blogs/seiko-mechanical-movements/about-seiko-kinetic-watches-and-seiko-kinetic-movement/|website=Strapcode.com}} These quartz watches use the motion of the wearer's wrist to charge their battery. === Grand Seiko 9F quartz movement === The 9F quartz movement is used in Grand Seiko quartz watches.{{Cite web |title=Quartz |url=https://www.grand-seiko.com/us-en/collections/movement/quartz |access-date=2024-07-05 |website=Grand Seiko |language=en-US}} The Grand Seiko's 9F quartz movement is assembled entirely by hand by two expert craftsmen. Features include: * Backlash auto-adjust mechanism * Twin pulse control motor * Instant date change mechanism – it can change the date display in 1/2000th of a second * Accuracy within +-10 seconds per year{{Cite web |title=Quartz |url=https://www.grand-seiko.com/us-en/collections/movement/quartz |access-date=2024-12-13 |website=Grand Seiko |language=en-US}} === Spring Drive === {{Main|Spring Drive}} [[File:Seiko Spacewalk.JPG|thumb|The Seiko Spacewalk is a limited edition Spring Drive model, designed specifically for use in space.]] The Spring Drive was announced in 1997, developed by Yoshikazu Akahane and his team, and inspired by Yoshikazu's vision: "a watch wound by a mainspring and with one-second-a-day accuracy, a precision that only the finest electronic watches could deliver."{{Cite web |title=History of Spring Drive |url=https://www.grand-seiko.com/instructions/html/GS_9R01_en/GOUMSYhtimjjif |access-date=2024-07-05 |website=www.grand-seiko.com}} The movement achieved high accuracy with one second per day, long power reserve (72 hours) with its unique developed alloy, fast winding with the "Magic Lever" design and glide-motion movement with the watch hands. Spring Drive combines a precision-regulating mechanism that uses a quartz crystal oscillator with a mainspring-driven mechanical watch, making it far more accurate than traditional mechanical watches. As of 2025, the Caliber 9RB2 has achieved an impressive accuracy of ±20 seconds per year. Spring Drive calibers are often superior not only in accuracy but also in power reserve compared to mechanical movements. The Caliber 9R01 offers a power reserve of 192 hours (eight days), while the 9RA2 and 9RA5 provide 120 hours (five days), and the 9R02 delivers 84 hours. These significantly exceed the 80-hour power reserve of Grand Seiko's longest-running mechanical movements, the 9SA4 and 9SA5.{{cite web|url=https://www.grand-seiko.com/us-en/collections/movement/springdrive|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250403134137/https://www.grand-seiko.com/us-en/collections/movement/springdrive|title=9R Spring Drive|publisher=Seiko|date=|archive-date=3 April 2025|access-date=20 April 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://deployant.com/grand-seiko-sbgd001/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006042652/https://deployant.com/grand-seiko-sbgd001/|title=Review: Grand Seiko SBGD001 Spring Drive 8 Day Power Reserve|publisher=Deployant|date=31 March 2025|archive-date=6 October 2024|access-date=20 April 2025}} The movement uses a [[mainspring]] as a source of energy and transmits it through a [[gear train]], just like a traditional mechanical watch, but instead of an escapement and balance wheel, Seiko used the newly developed "Tri-synchro regulator", which acts like a quartz movement. The Tri-synchro regulator has three main functions: controlling the mechanical energy of the mainspring, generate electricity for the low consumption (~25 nanowatts) quartz crystal oscillator and generate a magnetic force to regulate the glide wheel. By replacing the traditional [[escapement]] with a magnetic brake, the Spring Drive operates with lower noise and presents a glide motion hand that shows the continuous flow of time. The Spring Drive movement was also used as the basis for the first-ever watch designed to be worn by an astronaut during a space walk, the aptly named Seiko Spring Drive Spacewalk.{{Cite web |title=Seiko, Spacewalk, Commemorative Edition |url=https://www.gphg.org/en/watches/spacewalk-commemorative-edition |access-date=2024-07-05 |website=www.gphg.org |language=fr}} == Sponsorships == Seiko previously sponsored Honda F1 (formerly known as BAR [British American Racing] Honda). Seiko Group Corporation (セイコーグループ株式会社, Seikō Gurūpu kabushiki gaisha), commonly known as Seiko ( SAY-koh, Japanese: [seːkoː]), is a Japanese maker of watches, clocks, electronic devices, and semiconductors. Founded in 1881 by Kintarō Hattori in Tokyo, Seiko introduced the world's first commercial quartz wristwatch in 1969.
Seiko is widely known for its wristwatches. Seiko and Rolex are the only two watch companies considered to be vertically integrated. Seiko is able to design and develop all the components of a watch, as well as assemble, adjust, inspect and ship them in-house. Seiko's mechanical watches consist of approximately 200 parts, and the company has the technology and production facilities to design and manufacture all of these parts internally.
The company was incorporated (K. Hattori & Co., Ltd.) in 1917 and renamed Hattori Seiko Co., Ltd. in 1983 and Seiko Corporation in 1997. After reconstructing and creating its operating subsidiaries (such as Seiko Watch Corporation and Seiko Clock Inc.), it became a holding company in 2001 and was renamed Seiko Holdings Corporation on July 1, 2007. Seiko Holdings Corporation was renamed Seiko Group Corporation as of October 1, 2022.
Seiko watches were originally produced by two Hattori family companies (not subsidiaries of K. Hattori & Co); one was Daini Seikosha Co. (now known as Seiko Instruments Inc., a subsidiary of Seiko Holdings since 2009) and the other was Suwa Seikosha Co. (now known as Seiko Epson Corporation, an independent publicly traded company). Having two companies both producing the same brand of watch enabled Seiko to improve technology through competition and hedge risk. It also reduced risk of production problems, since one company can increase production in the case of decreased production in the other parties. Seiko remains as one of the world's most recognised watchmaking brands.
In Ginza, where the company was founded, there are several Seiko-related facilities in addition to Seiko House Ginza, including the Seiko Museum and Seiko Dream Square. Several Seiko boutiques and department stores in the area frequently offer Ginza-exclusive models.
